sketches.mechanism: An interface with no methods (a marker interface) — the body is intentionally empty, yet it changes how the system treats the object
sketches.resonance: Grief has no behavior, no methods you can call on it, yet simply carrying it changes everything about how the world processes you.

sketches.mechanism: The 'never' return type, which indicates a function that can never successfully return — combined with a void function that also never reaches its return
sketches.resonance: A promise to come back that the type system itself guarantees will never be fulfilled.

sketches.mechanism: Lua's weak references in tables — when nothing else holds onto a value, the garbage collector silently removes it, as if it was never there
sketches.resonance: A relationship that only exists as long as someone else remembers it; the moment all outside references are gone, it quietly ceases to exist.
sketches.draft:
local us = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "v" })

do
  local you = {}
  us[1] = you
end

collectgarbage()
-- us[1] is nil
